items.title: Section: Elemental Analysis Enters the Four Foundations — the Dissolution Sequence

items.zh: 臨捨命時，如前廣說至青瘀位，或復膿爛，即於膿爛發起種種流出勝解。漸漸膿流，展轉增廣，乃至大海、大地邊際，膿悉充滿。發起如是膿勝解已，次復發起火燒勝解。謂此身分無量無邊品類差別，為大火聚無量無邊品類燒燼。火既滅已，復起餘骨、餘灰勝解。復起無量無邊勝解，碎此骨灰以為細末。復起無量大風勝解，飄散此末，遍諸方維。既飄散已，不復觀見所飄灰骨及能飄風。唯觀有餘眇茫空界。
items.en: "As death approaches, as extensively explained before, up through the stage of discoloration, or further to decay — generate vivid understanding of pus flowing out from that decay. This pus flows further and further, spreading until it fills the great ocean and reaches the very limits of the earth. Having generated this understanding of pus, next generate the understanding of being consumed by fire … burned to ash by vast, boundless masses of flame of every kind. The fire having gone out, generate the understanding of remaining bone and ash … generate the understanding of a vast wind, scattering this ash in every direction and quarter. Once scattered, one no longer perceives either the scattered ash or the scattering wind — one perceives only the remaining, boundless space."

items.zh: 如是由其勝解作意，依於內外不淨加行，入界差別，於其身相住循身觀，從是趣入真實作意。謂由如是勝解作意，於內外身住循身觀。由勝解力，我此所作無量無邊水界、火界、地界、風界、虛空界相，我從無始生死流轉，所經諸界無量無邊，甚過於此。

items.title: Section: True-Reality Engagement — Tears, Milk, and Blood Exceeding the Four Oceans

items.zh: 謂由父母兄弟姊妹眷屬喪亡，及由親友財寶祿位離散失壞，悲泣雨淚。又飲母乳。又由作賊，擁逼劫掠，穿牆解結。由是因緣，遭無量度截手、刖足、斬頭、劓鼻，種種解割身諸支節，由是因緣，血流無量。如是所有淚、乳、血攝水界水聚，四大海水皆悉盈滿，於百分中不及其一。
items.en: "Through the deaths of parents, siblings, and family, and through the loss and ruin of friends, wealth, and position, I have wept tears like rain. I have also drunk my mother's milk. And through banditry, insurrection, and plunder … through these causes, I have suffered countless times the severing of hands, the cutting off of feet, beheading, the slicing of the nose, and every manner of bodily dismemberment. Through these causes, blood has flowed beyond measure. All such tears, milk, and blood, belonging to the water element, would entirely fill the four great oceans — and this is not even one hundredth of the true total."

items.zh: 又於諸有諸趣死生，經無量火焚燒尸骸，如是火聚亦無比況。又經無量棄捨骸骨，狼籍在地，亦無比況。又經無量風界生滅，分析尸骸，亦無比況。又經無量諸尸骸中眼等竅穴。又經無量諸識流轉。
items.en: "Further, across countless deaths and births in every mode and destiny of existence, my discarded corpses have been consumed by fire beyond counting — this mass of fire, too, is beyond comparison. Further, the bones I have discarded, scattered in disarray upon the ground, are likewise beyond comparison. Further, the wind that has arisen and ceased, dissolving my corpses, is likewise beyond comparison. Further, the very apertures — eyes and the rest — within my countless past corpses are beyond counting. Further, consciousness itself has transmigrated through countless such bodies without end."

items.zh: 後後尸骸新新發起，乃至今者最後尸骸，諸識流轉。如是安立後際諸趣，期限無定，如是乃至無量識界。

items.title: Section: Breath-Counting Applied — All Five Purifying-Conduct Objects Now Complete

items.zh: 又於阿那波那念正加行中，初修業者，先於舍宅前後窓門，或打鐵師、或鍛金銀師吹筒𣡖袋，或風外聚入出往來，善取相已；由緣於內入出息念，於入出息而起勝解。彼復先於微細息風，經心胸處麁穴往來而起勝解。然後漸漸於眾多風而起勝解。所謂乃至一切毛孔風皆隨入而起勝解。如是所有一切身分，風聚所隨、風聚所攝、風聚藏隱，無量風聚於中積集，如妬羅綿、或疊絮等諸輕飄物，於是諸相而起勝解。
items.en: "A beginner cultivating correct practice for mindfulness of the in-breath and out-breath first grasps the mark of wind at a house's doors and windows, or at a blacksmith's or goldsmith's bellows, or in the outer wind's coming and going; having grasped this, one generates vivid understanding of the in-breath and out-breath within. One first generates understanding of the subtle breath-wind … then gradually extends to understanding of wind throughout many places … until, throughout the entire body, wind pervades, is contained by, and lies hidden within every part — boundless wind gathered throughout, as light and drifting as cotton-down or wind-borne fluff — one generates vivid understanding of these marks."

items.zh: 彼若於內入息、出息流轉不絕作意思惟，爾時名為於其內身住循身觀。若復於他死尸骸中青瘀等位入息、出息流轉斷絕作意思惟，爾時名為於其外身住循身觀。若復於自臨欲死時而起勝解；或於已死入息、出息無有流轉而起勝解；或於未死入息、出息無有流轉而起勝解；由法爾故。爾時名為於內外身住循身觀。
items.en: "If one directs attention to the unbroken continuity of one's own in-breath and out-breath, this is called cultivating contemplation of the body with respect to the inner body. If one directs attention to the breath's cessation in another's corpse, in its stages of discoloration and so on, this is called cultivating contemplation of the body with respect to the outer body. And if one generates understanding of one's own approaching death; or of the breath's absence after death; or of the breath's natural absence even before death — as when one enters the fourth dhyāna, or during the earliest embryonic stages — this is called cultivating contemplation of the body with respect to both inner and outer."

items.zh: 遍於一切正加行中，應修如是止品助伴、止品所攝無倒加行。所餘一切，如前應知。

items.title: The Teacher's Summary: Ardent, Clearly Comprehending, Overcoming the World's Pull

items.zh: 如是所有初修業者，蒙正教誨修正行時，安住熾然，正知具念，調伏一切世間貪憂。若於如是正加行中，恒常修作、畢竟修作無倒作意，非諠鬧等所能動亂，是名熾然。若於如是正加行中，修奢摩他、毘鉢舍那，審諦了知亂不亂相，如是名為正知具念。若能善取諸厭離相、諸欣樂相，如是乃名調伏一切世間貪憂。
items.en: Thus, every beginner who, having received correct instruction, cultivates correct practice, abides ardent, with clear comprehension and mindfulness, overcoming all worldly craving and distress. Cultivating this correct practice constantly and to completion, with undistorted engagement, unshaken by clamour or anything else — this is called ardent. Cultivating calm-abiding and insight within this correct practice, carefully and truly knowing the disturbed and undisturbed marks — this is called clear comprehension joined with mindfulness. Skilfully grasping the marks of revulsion and of delight — this alone is called overcoming all worldly craving and distress.

items.zh: 由是因緣，宣說彼能安住熾然，乃至調伏世間貪憂。

blocks.text: The elements meditated on in dissolution, a famous reflection on how many tears we have shed, and the method applied to the breath. Two short passages are untranslated.

"As death approaches, through discoloration and decay, generate vivid understanding of pus flowing out; it flows further until it fills the great ocean." Then fire consuming it; then wind scattering the ash, until "one no longer perceives either the ash or the wind, only space".

"Through the deaths of parents, siblings, and family, and the loss of friends and wealth, I have wept tears like rain. I have drunk my mother's milk." Through violence, blood has been shed. "All such tears, milk, and blood would fill the four great oceans." And the fire that has burned my corpses, and the bones, would heap up like mountains.

"Grasp the mark of wind at a house's doors and windows, or at a smith's bellows"; then the breath within. "If one attends to the unbroken continuity of one's own breath, this is the inner body; if to the breath's cessation in another's corpse, the outer." Venerable Miào Jìng: one in the fourth absorption has no breath even before death.
"Thus every beginner who, having received correct instruction, cultivates correct practice, abides ardent, with clear comprehension and mindfulness, overcoming worldly craving and distress."

quiz.q: "As death approaches … generate understanding of pus flowing." Why does Master Cháng Bǎi call this confident-understanding engagement?
options: one isn't dying yet — one imagines the future moment of death
quiz.why: "As death approaches, as explained before, up through discoloration or decay — generate vivid understanding of pus flowing out." Master Cháng Bǎi: sitting in practice now, one hasn't reached death; one imagines what it will be like when life is relinquished — hence confident-understanding engagement.

quiz.q: Once the ash scatters, "one perceives only boundless space." How do the masters view this?
options: Miào Jìng: from here one enters true engagement, ultimate emptiness, space; Cháng Bǎi: it hasn't happened yet, but this contemplation breaks attachment
quiz.why: "Once scattered, one no longer perceives either the scattered ash or the scattering wind — one perceives only the remaining, boundless space." Venerable Miào Jìng: from here one enters true-reality engagement — ultimate emptiness, space. Master Cháng Bǎi: it hasn't happened yet, but one must contemplate this way to break one's attachment.

quiz.q: "Through banditry, 擁逼, and plunder." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain 擁逼?
options: not ordinary — having great power to overthrow a king and take the throne
quiz.why: "And through banditry, insurrection, and plunder." Venerable Miào Jìng: 擁逼 is not something ordinary people can do — one with vast power overthrows the king and becomes king.

quiz.q: Tears, milk, and blood "would fill the four oceans, not even one hundredth." What does Master Cháng Bǎi say of mother's milk?
options: the milk drunk is boundless — countless beings have been one's mother
quiz.why: "All such tears, milk, and blood, belonging to the water element, would entirely fill the four great oceans — and this is not even one hundredth." Master Cháng Bǎi: the mother's milk one has drunk is boundless; many beings have been one's mother.

quiz.q: Breath practice first grasps wind at "a smith's bellows." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain 橐?
options: a bottomless bag; generate understanding of wind — the breath is the body's inner wind
quiz.why: "Or at a blacksmith's or goldsmith's bellows, or in the outer wind's coming and going; having grasped this …" Master Cháng Bǎi: 橐 is a bag without a bottom; one should have understanding of wind — the breath is the inner body's wind.

quiz.q: "Or of the breath's absence even before death, by nature" — the English adds the fourth dhyāna and the embryo. What do the lectures say?
options: Miào Jìng: in the fourth dhyāna or in the womb, no breath yet alive; Cháng Bǎi: beings in the fourth dhyāna and above, and in the formless realm, have no breath
quiz.why: "Or of the breath's natural absence even before death." Venerable Miào Jìng: one who attains the fourth dhyāna has no breath yet isn't dead; or one in the womb. Master Cháng Bǎi: beings in the fourth dhyāna and above have no breath, nor do formless-realm beings. The English additions reflect this commentary.

quiz.q: "Unshaken by clamour — this is ardent." How does Venerable Miào Jìng describe it?
options: amid turmoil you're undisturbed — you have another world
quiz.why: "Cultivating this correct practice constantly and to completion, with undistorted engagement, unshaken by clamour or anything else — this is called ardent." Venerable Miào Jìng: amid a turbulent environment you aren't disturbed — you have another world.
